writes.rule: Per subtopic seen: pMastery 0.7 if right at D2/D3, 0.55 if right at D1, 0.25 if wrong; level L0-L3 from the ladder step reached
Prerequisite-gap index = 100 x weighted misses / weighted items seen in slots 1-4, averaged over groups
Groups with the highest Part A percent (top 1-2, only if >= 65%)
Groups with the lowest Part A percent (bottom 1-2, only if < 65%)
Calibration = 1 - mean |confidence/5 - correct| over Part A (feeds the first MCI reading)
Highest difficulty answered correctly twice in a row: D1 low, D2 medium, D3 high
Verbal reasoning = percent of Part B verbal items right
Numerical reasoning = percent of Part B numerical items right
Abstract reasoning = percent of Part B abstract items right
Spatial reasoning = percent of Part B spatial items right
Logical deduction = percent right on Part B items tagged p65
Numeracy fluency = numerical percent scaled by speed (right answers under target time count 1.2x, max 100)
Processing speed = 100 x share of Part B items answered right within target seconds
RIASEC profile: each career-interest item scored 1-5; letter score = mean of its 2 items; top 3 letters form the code (e.g. IRC)

items.stem: Factorise x² + 5x + 6.
items.markingKey: C. (x + 2)(x + 3). Find two numbers that multiply to 6 and add to 5

items.stem: What is the gradient of the line y = 3x - 2?
items.subtopicHint: Gradient and intercept of a straight line
items.markingKey: C. 3. In y = mx + c, m is the gradient

items.stem: What is the gradient of the line through (1, 2) and (4, 11)?
items.subtopicHint: Gradient and intercept of a straight line

items.stem: A bag holds 3 red and 5 blue counters. One is picked at random. What is the probability it is red?
items.subtopicHint: Probability of equally likely and combined outcomes
items.markingKey: B. 3/8. 3 red out of 8 counters

items.stem: A fair die is rolled. What is the probability of getting a number greater than 4?
items.subtopicHint: Probability of equally likely and combined outcomes
items.markingKey: A. 1/3. Only 5 and 6 work: 2 out of 6

items.stem: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
items.subtopicHint: Probability of equally likely and combined outcomes
items.markingKey: B. 3/4. HH, HT, TH out of HH, HT, TH, TT

items.stem: What is the mean of 4, 7, 9, 12 and 8?
What is the median of 3, 9, 4, 7, 12 and 5?
items.markingKey: B. 6. Order: 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12; middle pair (5 + 7) ÷ 2

items.stem: The mean of five numbers is 12. One number, 20, is removed. What is the mean of the other four?
What is 9^(1/2)?
items.markingKey: D. 3. A power of ½ is a square root

items.stem: Simplify √50.
What is 8^(2/3)?
items.markingKey: D. 4. Cube root of 8 is 2, then square it

items.stem: What is the next term of 5, 9, 13, 17, ...?
items.markingKey: C. 21. The common difference is 4

items.stem: An arithmetic sequence starts 3, 8, 13, ... What is the 20th term?
What is the sum of the first 10 terms of 2, 5, 8, ...?
1000 is invested at 10% compound interest per year. What is it worth after 2 years?
A phone worth 20 000 loses 20% of its value each year. What is it worth after 2 years?
Which grows faster over 10 years: 5% simple interest or 5% compound interest on the same amount?
items.answer: Compound, because interest is earned on earlier interest
options: Simple, because the rate is fixed
Simple, because it is added every year
Compound, because interest is earned on earlier interest
items.markingKey: D. Compound, because interest is earned on earlier interest. Compound growth multiplies

items.subtopicHint: Solving quadratic equations and the discriminant
items.markingKey: A. x = 4 or x = -1. Set each bracket to zero

items.stem: How many real solutions does x² + 2x + 5 = 0 have?
items.subtopicHint: Solving quadratic equations and the discriminant
items.markingKey: A. none. Discriminant 4 - 20 = -16 < 0

items.stem: For what value of k does x² - 6x + k = 0 have exactly one solution?
items.subtopicHint: Solving quadratic equations and the discriminant
items.markingKey: A. 9. Discriminant 36 - 4k = 0

items.stem: A 1200 kg car accelerates at 2 m/s². What resultant force acts on it?
Sodium has the electron arrangement 2,8,1. How many electrons are in its outer shell?
items.markingKey: B. 1. The last number is the outer shell

items.stem: An element has the electron arrangement 2,8,7. What happens when it forms an ion?
items.answer: It gains one electron to form a 1- ion
options: It loses seven electrons to form a 7+ ion
It loses one electron to form a 1+ ion
It gains one electron to form a 1- ion
items.markingKey: C. It gains one electron to form a 1- ion. Gaining one electron completes the outer shell (chlorine)

items.stem: Magnesium forms Mg²⁺ ions and oxygen forms O²⁻ ions. What is the formula of magnesium oxide?
items.markingKey: A. MgO. The charges balance one to one

items.stem: Aluminium forms Al³⁺ ions and oxygen forms O²⁻ ions. What is the formula of aluminium oxide?
items.markingKey: C. Al₂O₃. 2 x (+3) balances 3 x (-2)

items.stem: Which equation is correctly balanced?
items.markingKey: A. 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃. Count atoms: 4 Fe and 6 O on each side

items.stem: A cyclist speeds up from 0 to 20 m/s in 5 s. What is the acceleration?
items.markingKey: D. 4 m/s². a = change in velocity ÷ time

items.stem: On a velocity-time graph, what does the area under the line show?
items.markingKey: B. The distance travelled. Area = velocity x time

items.stem: A car moving at 20 m/s brakes steadily to rest in 4 s. How far does it travel while braking?
items.markingKey: B. 40 m. Area of the triangle: ½ x 4 x 20

items.stem: Natural selection depends on
items.markingKey: B. variation within a population. Without variation there is nothing to select

items.stem: Why are individuals with useful variations more likely to pass them on?
items.answer: They are more likely to survive and reproduce
options: They decide to have more offspring
They are more likely to survive and reproduce
items.markingKey: C. They are more likely to survive and reproduce. Survival of the fittest

items.stem: Peppered moths became mostly dark in industrial areas of 19th-century England. What best explains this?
items.answer: Dark moths were better camouflaged on sooty trees, so fewer were eaten by birds
options: Dark moths were better camouflaged on sooty trees, so fewer were eaten by birds
The moths chose to turn dark
items.markingKey: A. Dark moths were better camouflaged on sooty trees, so fewer were eaten by birds. Selection by predation

items.stem: Antibiotics are used to treat infections caused by
items.markingKey: D. bacteria. They do not work on viruses

items.stem: Why should a patient finish a full course of antibiotics?
items.answer: To kill all the bacteria so resistant ones do not survive and spread
options: To make the medicine taste better
To kill all the bacteria so resistant ones do not survive and spread
items.markingKey: D. To kill all the bacteria so resistant ones do not survive and spread. Stopping early leaves the toughest bacteria

items.stem: MRSA is a strain of bacteria resistant to many antibiotics. How did it most likely arise?
items.answer: Random mutations gave some bacteria resistance, and antibiotic use selected them
options: Bacteria learned to resist on purpose
Random mutations gave some bacteria resistance, and antibiotic use selected them
items.markingKey: D. Random mutations gave some bacteria resistance, and antibiotic use selected them. Natural selection in action

items.stem: In a food chain, plants are
items.markingKey: B. producers. They make food by photosynthesis

items.stem: Why are food chains rarely longer than five links?
items.answer: Energy is lost at each trophic level, mostly as heat
options: Energy is lost at each trophic level, mostly as heat
items.markingKey: B. Energy is lost at each trophic level, mostly as heat. Only about 10% passes on

items.stem: A field has 10 000 kJ of energy in its grass. About how much reaches the secondary consumers?
items.markingKey: B. 100 kJ. About 10% per step, twice

items.stem: Which process removes carbon dioxide from the air?
items.markingKey: B. photosynthesis. Plants take in CO₂

items.stem: How do decomposers return carbon to the atmosphere?
items.answer: They respire as they break down dead matter, releasing CO₂
options: They absorb it from the soil
They store it as fossil fuels instantly
They respire as they break down dead matter, releasing CO₂
items.markingKey: D. They respire as they break down dead matter, releasing CO₂. Decay is respiration by microbes

items.stem: Why does large-scale deforestation increase atmospheric CO₂?
items.answer: Fewer trees remove CO₂, and burning or decay of the trees releases it
options: Fewer trees remove CO₂, and burning or decay of the trees releases it
items.markingKey: B. Fewer trees remove CO₂, and burning or decay of the trees releases it. Two effects add up

items.stem: Read: "Meera glanced at the clock again, tapped her pen and read the same line for the fifth time." How is Meera most likely feeling?
items.markingKey: D. Restless and unable to concentrate. Repeated glancing and rereading suggest restlessness

items.stem: In 'The wind howled through the empty streets', the wind is given a human or animal quality. This is
items.markingKey: A. personification. An object is given living qualities

items.stem: What is the effect of 'the classroom was a pressure cooker before the exam'?
items.answer: It shows the tension was building and about to burst
options: It shows the students were hungry
It shows the tension was building and about to burst
It shows the classroom was hot from cooking
It shows the exam was easy
items.markingKey: B. It shows the tension was building and about to burst. A pressure cooker builds pressure until it releases

items.stem: In an argument, the main point the writer wants you to accept is the
items.markingKey: C. claim. Evidence supports the claim

items.stem: Which sentence is a counterargument in an essay arguing for school uniforms?
items.answer: Some say uniforms limit students' self-expression.
options: Uniforms reduce peer pressure about clothes.
A 2023 survey found most parents support uniforms.
Some say uniforms limit students' self-expression.
items.markingKey: D. Some say uniforms limit students' self-expression.. A counterargument presents the opposing view

items.stem: A writer says: 'Everyone I know hates homework, so homework should be banned.' What is the main weakness?
items.answer: The evidence is a small, personal sample
options: It is written in the first person
The evidence is a small, personal sample
items.markingKey: D. The evidence is a small, personal sample. A few friends do not represent everyone

items.stem: Which of these is a complex sentence?
items.answer: When the bell rang, the students rushed out.
options: When the bell rang, the students rushed out.
The bell rang and the students rushed out.
items.markingKey: B. When the bell rang, the students rushed out.. It has a main clause and a subordinate clause

items.stem: A story reads: 'The door creaked. Silence. Then footsteps.' What is the effect of the short sentences?
options: They make the story feel relaxed
They show the writer ran out of ideas
They explain the setting in detail
items.markingKey: D. They build tension and suspense. Short, broken sentences slow the reader and create suspense

items.stem: Rearrange into a correct sentence: "the / finally / after / rain / match / the / began / the / stopped"
items.answer: The match finally began after the rain stopped.
options: The match stopped after the rain finally began.
The rain finally began after the match stopped.
The match finally began after the rain stopped.
After the match finally began the rain stopped.
items.markingKey: C. The match finally began after the rain stopped.. The match could only start once the rain had stopped

items.stem: An appeal to the audience's emotions is called
items.markingKey: A. pathos. Pathos is emotion

items.stem: 'As a doctor for twenty years, I have seen the harm smoking does.' Which appeal is this?
items.markingKey: C. ethos. It builds the speaker's credibility

items.stem: A speaker says: 'Ninety per cent of plastic is never recycled. Picture a sea turtle tangled in it.' Which appeals are combined?
items.markingKey: A. logos then pathos. A statistic, then an emotional image

items.stem: 'We will fight, we will endure, we will win' uses
items.markingKey: A. tricolon (a rule of three). Three parallel parts

items.stem: Repeating 'I have a dream' at the start of several sentences is called
items.markingKey: A. anaphora. Repetition at the start of clauses

items.stem: What is the effect of the antithesis in 'Ask not what your country can do for you; ask what you can do for your country'?
items.answer: The reversal makes the call to duty memorable and challenges the audience
options: It confuses the audience on purpose
The reversal makes the call to duty memorable and challenges the audience
It lists facts about the country
It adds humour to a serious speech
items.markingKey: B. The reversal makes the call to duty memorable and challenges the audience. Contrasting halves create emphasis

items.stem: The purpose of a persuasive speech is mainly to
items.answer: convince the audience to think or act in a certain way
items.subtopicHint: Audience, purpose and context of a speech
options: convince the audience to think or act in a certain way
items.markingKey: A. convince the audience to think or act in a certain way. Persuade

items.stem: A speech to a youth climate rally would most likely use
items.subtopicHint: Audience, purpose and context of a speech
items.markingKey: C. direct address, urgency and inclusive "we". Fit language to audience

items.stem: Why might the same speech be received differently 50 years after it was given?
items.answer: The historical context and audience values have changed
items.subtopicHint: Audience, purpose and context of a speech
options: Speeches lose all meaning over time
The historical context and audience values have changed
items.markingKey: D. The historical context and audience values have changed. Meaning depends on context

items.stem: A story told using 'I' by a character in it has a
items.subtopicHint: Narrative voice and point of view
items.markingKey: A. first-person narrator. The narrator is 'I'

items.stem: A narrator looking back on childhood as an adult is called a
items.subtopicHint: Narrative voice and point of view
items.markingKey: B. retrospective narrator. They narrate with hindsight

items.stem: What is a key effect of a limited first-person narrator in a coming-of-age novel?
items.answer: Readers share the narrator's growing understanding and may see more than the narrator does
items.subtopicHint: Narrative voice and point of view
options: Readers share the narrator's growing understanding and may see more than the narrator does
items.markingKey: B. Readers share the narrator's growing understanding and may see more than the narrator does. Limited view creates dramatic irony

items.stem: Which leader is most associated with the unification of Germany in 1871?
items.markingKey: C. Bismarck. Prussian chief minister

items.stem: The Berlin Conference of 1884-85 was held to
items.answer: set rules for European powers claiming African territory
options: set rules for European powers claiming African territory
items.markingKey: A. set rules for European powers claiming African territory. It divided Africa among Europeans

items.stem: Why were African borders drawn at the Berlin Conference later a source of conflict?
items.answer: They ignored ethnic and cultural groups living in those areas
options: They gave every group its own country
They ignored ethnic and cultural groups living in those areas
items.markingKey: D. They ignored ethnic and cultural groups living in those areas. Arbitrary borders split and combined peoples

items.stem: When demand is greater than supply at the current price, there is a
items.subtopicHint: Price determination: equilibrium, shortages and surpluses
items.markingKey: D. shortage. Buyers want more than is available

items.stem: If there is a surplus of mangoes, what usually happens to the price?
items.subtopicHint: Price determination: equilibrium, shortages and surpluses
items.markingKey: D. It falls. Sellers cut prices to clear stock

items.stem: Concert tickets sell out within minutes and resell online for triple the price. What does this suggest?
items.answer: The original price was set below equilibrium
items.subtopicHint: Price determination: equilibrium, shortages and surpluses
options: The original price was set below equilibrium
There was a surplus of tickets
items.markingKey: B. The original price was set below equilibrium. A shortage shows price below equilibrium

items.stem: In first past the post, a candidate wins a seat by
items.answer: getting more votes than any other candidate
options: getting over 50% of all votes nationally
getting more votes than any other candidate
items.markingKey: B. getting more votes than any other candidate. A simple plurality

items.stem: Proportional representation aims to
items.answer: give parties seats in proportion to their share of the vote
options: give parties seats in proportion to their share of the vote
give all seats to the largest party
items.markingKey: A. give parties seats in proportion to their share of the vote. Seats match votes

items.stem: Party A wins 40% of votes nationally but 60% of seats under first past the post. Why can this happen?
items.answer: It narrowly wins many constituencies, and votes for losing candidates win nothing
options: It narrowly wins many constituencies, and votes for losing candidates win nothing
items.markingKey: C. It narrowly wins many constituencies, and votes for losing candidates win nothing. Winner-takes-all in each seat

items.stem: Which of these is a long-term cause of the First World War?
items.subtopicHint: Long-term causes of the First World War
items.markingKey: B. the alliance system. MAIN: militarism, alliances, imperialism, nationalism

items.stem: The naval race before 1914 was mainly between
items.subtopicHint: Long-term causes of the First World War
items.markingKey: C. Britain and Germany. Both built Dreadnought battleships

items.stem: How did the alliance system turn a local Balkan crisis into a world war?
items.answer: Countries were bound to defend allies, so one war pulled in others
items.subtopicHint: Long-term causes of the First World War
options: Countries were bound to defend allies, so one war pulled in others
It prevented any country from joining
items.markingKey: A. Countries were bound to defend allies, so one war pulled in others. Commitments spread the conflict

items.stem: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in
items.subtopicHint: The Treaty of Versailles: terms and reactions
items.markingKey: B. 1919. After the armistice of 1918

items.stem: Which of these was a term of the treaty?
items.subtopicHint: The Treaty of Versailles: terms and reactions
items.markingKey: B. Germany had to pay reparations. Payments for war damage

items.stem: Why did many Germans call the treaty a "Diktat"?
items.answer: Germany was not allowed to negotiate the terms
items.subtopicHint: The Treaty of Versailles: terms and reactions
options: Germany was not allowed to negotiate the terms
items.markingKey: C. Germany was not allowed to negotiate the terms. A dictated peace

items.stem: In a democracy, governments are chosen through
items.markingKey: D. free elections. Power comes from the people

items.stem: Which ideology called for the state to own the means of production?
items.markingKey: D. communism. Based on Marx

items.stem: What did fascism and communism have in common in the 1930s?
items.answer: Both used one-party states and suppressed opposition
options: Both used one-party states and suppressed opposition
items.markingKey: B. Both used one-party states and suppressed opposition. Both were authoritarian

items.stem: Stalin's plans to rapidly build industry were called
items.markingKey: D. Five-Year Plans. Targets set by the state

items.stem: Collectivisation meant
items.answer: small farms were merged into large state-controlled farms
options: farms were sold to private owners
small farms were merged into large state-controlled farms
items.markingKey: D. small farms were merged into large state-controlled farms. Land was taken into collective farms

items.stem: Why did collectivisation cause a famine in Ukraine in 1932-33?
items.answer: Grain was seized for the state and resisting peasants were punished
options: Grain was seized for the state and resisting peasants were punished
items.markingKey: B. Grain was seized for the state and resisting peasants were punished. Forced requisitioning

items.stem: What number comes next? 5, 10, 20, 40, ?

The average of five numbers is 18. Four of them are 15, 20, 12 and 25. What is the fifth?
A price rises by 20% and then falls by 20%. What is the overall change?
Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to 'scarce'?
Doctor is to hospital as teacher is to ...
No reptiles have fur. All snakes are reptiles. Which conclusion follows?
items.explanation: Snakes are inside the reptile group, which has no fur; the last option may be true but does not follow

items.stem: Five friends sit in a row. P is at one end and Q sits next to P. R is in the middle seat. S does not sit next to R. Where does T sit?
items.explanation: Seats 1-5: P, Q, R; S cannot be in 4, so S is in 5 and T in 4

items.stem: Which letter comes next? Z, X, V, T, ?
items.explanation: Go back two letters each time

items.stem: In a code, CAT is written DBU. How is DOG written?
items.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward

items.stem: An arrow turns 90° clockwise at each step. Step 1 points up, step 2 right, step 3 down. Which way does it point at step 6?
items.explanation: The cycle repeats every 4 steps; step 6 = step 2

items.stem: In a 3 x 3 grid every row and column has one circle, one square and one triangle. Row 1: circle, square, triangle. Row 2: triangle, circle, square. What goes in row 3, column 2?
items.explanation: Column 2 already has a square and a circle

items.explanation: A cone has a circular base and an apex

items.explanation: This is one of the 11 nets of a cube

items.stem: A wall clock seen in a mirror appears to show 3:00. What is the real time?
items.explanation: A mirror swaps left and right: 3 becomes 9

items.stem: A 4 cm cube is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have no paint at all?
items.explanation: The unpainted core is 2 x 2 x 2
